title: Use your Android phone as a Google TV remote: setup and limits
description: Pair the Google TV app with your TV using its on-screen code, check the controls that work, and understand where The Remote's Android app fits.
body:
# Use your Android phone as a Google TV remote: setup and limits

Use the Google TV Android app on the TV’s home Wi-Fi, select your Android TV or Google TV, then pair with its on-screen code. [Google's Android TV remote guide](https://support.google.com/androidtv/answer/6122465?hl=en)

Before putting the physical remote away, try navigation, typing and the sound controls you use most.

## Check the device behind the screen

Here, **Google TV app** means the app on your phone. **Google TV device** means the TV or streaming device you want to control.

Find the model in the device's settings, manual, or product label and look up the manufacturer's platform specification. A brand name alone isn't a compatibility check. If an HDMI-connected box supplies your TV interface, identify that box too.

Google's remote instructions cover Android TV and Google TV. Its streaming-device instructions specifically include Chromecast with Google TV and Google TV Streamer. Don't extend that list to every device with Chromecast or Android in its name. [Google's streaming-device remote guide](https://support.google.com/chromecast/answer/11221499?hl=en)

Keep the TV switched on and, for a separate streamer, select its HDMI input. You need to see the pairing code.

If the TV is brand new or still connected to an old network, finish its setup first. Some Google TV models offer a phone-assisted initial setup, but the supported route varies. Follow the screen and the manufacturer's instructions rather than expecting the virtual remote to fix an unconfigured connection. [Google TV initial setup options](https://support.google.com/googletv/answer/10050221?hl=en)

## Pair the Google TV app

Install or update [Google TV from Google LLC on Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.google.android.videos&hl=en). The listing will show whether it's available for your phone and region.

For this Wi-Fi walkthrough, confirm that the phone and TV use the same home network. Open the TV's network settings to check; working internet on each device isn't enough to verify the local connection. [Google's virtual-remote network check](https://support.google.com/googletv/answer/15766805?hl=en)

1. Open the Google TV app on your Android phone
2. Tap the TV connection button near the bottom-right of the app. Google's pages use **Connect TV** or a nearby-TV count for this entry point
3. Choose the TV or streamer you intend to control
4. Copy the pairing code from that TV screen into the phone app
5. Tap **Pair**, then try moving the selection on the TV

These are Google's documented steps. The connection-button wording varies across its help pages, so use the TV connection entry point visible in your version. [Google TV pairing instructions](https://support.google.com/googletv/answer/11136134?co=GENIE.Platform%3DAndroid&hl=en)

If several devices appear, check the selected name before entering a code. If none appears, compare the network connections before starting over. If the app rejects the code, check the screen again rather than reusing one from a previous attempt.

## Check the controls you'll actually use

Google describes navigation, media playback, and phone-keyboard input among the virtual remote's functions. Use a short check on your setup before assuming every TV app behaves alike. [Google's description of basic controls](https://support.google.com/chromecast/answer/11221499?hl=en)

**Navigation:** Move between a few items, open one, then return with Back or Home. Watch the TV so you know you're controlling the intended device.

**Typing:** Open the search field you want to use and try a harmless phrase. Check that the right text reaches the right field. If navigation works but typing fails in one app, keep that distinction when troubleshooting.

**Playback:** Try pause and resume in the app you normally watch. Check each player you use regularly.

**Sound:** Check volume at a comfortable level. Note which device produces it: the TV, a soundbar, or a receiver.

Keep the original remote within reach for any controls that don't respond.

## Where the limits matter

### Volume and power depend on the setup

A physical streaming-device remote can control equipment through a different path from a phone app. Google documents infrared behavior for its Voice Remotes and separate volume settings for the streamer, TV, and external audio equipment. If phone navigation works but volume doesn't, investigate that audio path before pairing everything again. [Voice Remote control paths](https://support.google.com/chromecast/answer/12934376?hl=en), [Google's volume setup](https://support.google.com/chromecast/answer/10094150?hl=en)

### Remote control and casting do different jobs

The virtual remote sends control actions. Casting chooses media for a compatible receiver; [screen mirroring displays the phone's screen](https://support.google.com/chromecast/answer/6059461?hl=en). Choose the route that matches what you want to put on the screen. [Google TV remote and casting instructions](https://support.google.com/googletv/answer/11136134?co=GENIE.Platform%3DAndroid&hl=en)

### A phone remote still needs a reachable device

The same-network setup described here isn't an away-from-home control service. A hotel or guest network may also block communication between connected devices. Ask the network owner about supported access instead of changing security settings at random. [Google's streaming-device network limitations](https://support.google.com/chromecast/answer/7566322?hl=en-CA)

## Where The Remote fits

The Remote is a separate, free Android phone app. It's built for compatible Android TV and Google TV devices on your home network, with Android TV Remote Service v2 required. Available controls vary by model.

You can enter a YouTube search on your phone, review a shared YouTube link before sending it, name saved TVs by room, and choose app-specific controls. YouTube behavior also depends on the TV and its YouTube version. [See The Remote's features and requirements](https://baagad-ai.github.io/TVRemote-site/)

The Remote needs no app account. [Download The Remote APK](https://baagad-ai.github.io/TVRemote-site/#download) when available. No signup or email is needed. Check compatibility before installing; a phone remote still needs a reachable TV on your home network.
summary: Pair your phone and check the controls you actually use.

title: Android TV remote app can't find your TV? Start here
description: TV missing, pairing code absent, or controls doing nothing? Check the right connection problem on Android TV and Google TV before changing settings.
body:
# Android TV remote app can't find your TV? Start here

Start with what you can see. A TV that never appears in the phone app needs a different check from one that pairs successfully but won't accept a search. Before changing anything, turn on the TV, check that you're looking at the right TV or streaming-device input, and confirm its network connection.

Then choose your starting point:

- **No TV listed:** check the device and its network
- **TV listed, pairing incomplete:** check the selected screen and pairing code
- **Paired, but an action fails:** test navigation separately from typing, volume, or playback

These checks focus on compatible Android TV and Google TV devices. The pairing instructions below are for Google's Google TV phone app; other apps can use different screens.

## If your TV never appears

### Check what you're trying to control

Find the TV or streaming device's model in its settings, manual, or product label, then check the manufacturer's specifications for its platform. A familiar TV brand or a working YouTube app doesn't identify the operating system.

Google documents its phone remote for Android TV and Google TV. Its separate streaming-device guide names Chromecast with Google TV and Google TV Streamer. An older Cast-only Chromecast shouldn't be treated as the same device. [Google's supported remote setup](https://support.google.com/chromecast/answer/11221499?hl=en)

If you use a streaming box, check that box's connection as well as the TV. The screen can be on while the box you're trying to control is off or showing on another input.

### Compare the actual connections

Open the phone's Wi-Fi settings and the TV's network settings. For the documented Wi-Fi setup, both should use the same network. On Google TV, Google directs you to **Settings → Network & Internet**. Menu names on other devices can differ. [Google's network check](https://support.google.com/googletv/answer/15766805?hl=en)

Check these details before blaming the app:

- Is the phone using mobile data while the TV uses home Wi-Fi?
- Did one device join a guest network?
- Does the TV still remember a network from your previous home?
- If the TV uses Ethernet, does its cable lead to the home network your phone uses? Record that wired setup when asking for help; the Wi-Fi-only instructions don't establish compatibility for every Ethernet configuration

A video loading on both devices proves they can reach the internet. It doesn't prove they can reach each other locally.

Different Wi-Fi bands aren't an automatic diagnosis. Google notes that most routers let devices on 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz communicate. Check the network arrangement before changing bands. [Google's explanation of cross-band communication](https://support.google.com/googlenest/answer/10634602?hl=en-SG)

### Know when the network needs its owner

Guest, hotel, school, and managed networks may separate connected devices. Google documents client-isolation and web-sign-in limitations for its streaming devices. If you're on someone else's network, ask its owner whether local device communication is supported. Keep router security settings intact while you establish the cause. [Google's streaming-device network guidance](https://support.google.com/chromecast/answer/7566322?hl=en-CA)

If the TV hasn't joined the network at all, restore that connection first using its original remote or a control route supported by the manufacturer.

## If the TV appears but won't pair

In the Google TV phone app, choose your TV from the TV connection button. Enter the code on that screen and tap **Pair**. Google’s Android TV guide labels it **Connect TV**. [Google's pairing instructions](https://support.google.com/androidtv/answer/6122465?hl=en)

**No code visible?** Check the selected device name against the screen in front of you. With several TVs or a plugged-in streamer, it's easy to look at the wrong display or input. Return to device selection and try the intended device again.

**Code rejected?** Use the code currently on that screen. If pairing restarts, don't keep entering a code you copied from an earlier attempt.

Seeing a device in a Cast menu or seeing media controls in Google Home isn't enough to establish that a full remote pairing has completed. Use the remote's pairing flow as your check.

## If it pairs but something doesn't work

Try moving the selection, then Back or Home. Watch whether the TV responds.

If navigation works, write down the action that fails. Test typing in the intended search field with a harmless phrase. If it fails only in one TV app, report that app and field rather than describing the entire connection as broken.

For volume, note whether sound comes from the TV, a receiver, or a soundbar. Google's guidance explains that the streaming device and external audio equipment can have separate volume settings. A working navigation control doesn't settle the audio path. [Google's volume-control guidance](https://support.google.com/chromecast/answer/10094150?hl=en)

## Try a supported restart, then collect the useful details

If the basic checks don't help, restart the TV or streamer using its official instructions. Google TV provides **Settings → System → Restart** where that menu is available. Let any active software update finish first. [Google TV restart guidance](https://support.google.com/googletv/answer/10070482?hl=en)

Afterward, reopen the phone app and retry once. For support, collect:

- Phone model, Android version, and remote-app version
- TV or streamer model and software version
- Wi-Fi or Ethernet connection, including whether it's a guest network
- The exact failure stage and which controls still work
- What changed before the problem started and what you've already tried

Leave passwords and account details out of screenshots. This is more useful than a list of resets that changed several things at once.

## Trying The Remote

The Remote is a free Android phone app for compatible Android TV and Google TV devices. It uses your home network and requires Android TV Remote Service v2; controls vary by model.

The Remote needs no app account. [Download The Remote APK](https://baagad-ai.github.io/TVRemote-site/#download) when available. No signup or email is needed. Check compatibility before installing; a phone remote still needs a reachable TV on your home network.
summary: Find the failure stage before pairing everything again.

title: How to type on Android TV with your phone
description: Use your Android phone to type on Android TV or Google TV. Pair the remote, try a text field, and troubleshoot a missing keyboard or text that won’t appear.
body:
# How to type on Android TV with your phone

You can use the Google TV app on an Android phone to enter text on a compatible Android TV or Google TV. Pair the phone with the TV, open a text field on the TV, then try the phone keyboard. Google supports phone-based text entry, but a working direction pad alone doesn’t tell you whether a particular app’s search field will accept it. [Google’s remote features](https://support.google.com/googletv/answer/11136134?co=GENIE.Platform%3DAndroid&hl=en)

Start with a short search. Once you can see those letters arrive, type the long title.

## Connect the phone first

Put the phone and TV on the same home Wi-Fi, with the TV switched on. This route is for Android TV and Google TV. [Android TV setup requirements](https://support.google.com/androidtv/answer/6122465?hl=en)

Open the Google TV app, choose your TV from the connection button, enter the code on the TV and tap **Pair**. Google’s Android TV guide labels it **Connect TV**. [Google’s pairing guide](https://support.google.com/androidtv/answer/6122465?hl=en)

Before going further, use a direction button and watch the TV highlight move. If you have more than one TV, this is also a useful check that you selected the right one.

## Try one short search

Use the remote controls to open the TV app you want, move to its search field and select it. Look for an active text-entry field, rather than leaving the search icon highlighted.

When the phone offers its keyboard, enter a short word such as “jazz”. If your remote screen has a keyboard control, open it. Watch the TV: did the text arrive in the intended field? If it did, finish the query and use the available search or submit control.

If that field ignores the phone keyboard, use the checks below to find out whether the problem follows the field or the whole connection. [Google’s phone-keyboard guidance](https://support.google.com/chromecast/answer/11221499?hl=en)

## If the keyboard is missing

First, select the TV’s text field again. A page containing a search box isn’t the same as a box ready to receive text.

If you opened the remote from Android’s Quick Settings, try opening the Google TV app itself. Choose the same TV and revisit the same field. Google supports both entry points, so this gives you another way to reach the remote. [Google’s remote entry points](https://support.google.com/chromecast/answer/11221499?hl=en)

Keep the TV app and search field unchanged during this comparison. Otherwise, you won’t know whether the difference came from the phone’s remote screen or the TV app.

## If the keyboard appears but nothing arrives

Try the same short word in a second TV app’s text field. Then compare the results:

- **Typing works in one field:** you’ve found a working text-entry route. Note which app or field failed; don’t start changing the router because of that one result.
- **Typing fails in both, but navigation works:** record the two failures separately from the working direction controls. That is more useful for support than “the remote doesn’t work”.
- **Navigation also fails:** go back to the connection check. Confirm the selected TV and network before investigating individual apps.

For an unresponsive connection, Google recommends a TV restart: unplug, wait ten seconds, reconnect, then pair again. Let software updates finish first, and check that nobody is watching. [Google’s virtual-remote troubleshooting](https://support.google.com/googletv/answer/15766805?hl=en)

## Still stuck? Capture the useful details

Write down the phone model, Android version, TV or streamer model, remote app version, and the exact TV app and field that failed. Include whether the keyboard was missing, whether letters appeared, and whether navigation still worked. Use a harmless sample query in any screenshot.

For Google TV app feedback, open your profile picture, choose **Help & feedback**, then **Send feedback**. Review what you’re sending and keep passwords out of the report. [Google’s feedback instructions](https://support.google.com/googletv/answer/9654581?hl=en)

## A phone-first option

The Remote includes a phone-entered YouTube search that you send to a selected compatible Android TV or Google TV over your home network. It requires Android TV Remote Service v2; whether the TV accepts the search depends on the device and its YouTube version. Its dedicated YouTube search is useful when that’s the task you came to do. [The Remote’s compatibility and search details](https://baagad-ai.github.io/TVRemote-site/#compatibility)

The Remote needs no app account. [Download The Remote APK](https://baagad-ai.github.io/TVRemote-site/#download) when available. No signup or email is needed. Check compatibility before installing; a phone remote still needs a reachable TV on your home network.
summary: Get the right letters into the right search field.

title: Search YouTube on your TV with your Android phone
description: Type a YouTube query on your Android phone. Choose between browsing results on the TV, selecting a video on your phone and The Remote.
body:
# Search YouTube on your TV with your Android phone

You have two useful routes: enter text into YouTube’s TV search with a compatible phone remote, or find a video in the YouTube phone app and send that video to the TV. Choose based on where you want to browse the results.

A query such as “live jazz” leaves the next choice open. A video you’ve already selected gives the TV something specific to play.

## Browse the results on the TV

Google’s remote supports text entry on Android TV and Google TV. Whether it reaches YouTube’s search field depends on that field accepting the input. [Google’s remote features](https://support.google.com/googletv/answer/11136134?co=GENIE.Platform%3DAndroid&hl=en)

1. Pair the Google TV phone app using the code on your TV. For this Wi-Fi setup, both devices need the same home network. [Google’s pairing guide](https://support.google.com/androidtv/answer/6122465?hl=en)
2. Open YouTube on the TV and select its search field. The field needs to be active, rather than the search icon merely highlighted.
3. If the phone remote offers its keyboard, enter a short query such as “jazz”. Watch for the letters on the TV.
4. If they arrive correctly, submit the search and use the remote to browse the TV’s results.

If navigation works but the text doesn’t arrive, try another TV app’s search field. A second working field is a useful clue that the first app handles input differently. Keep those results separate when asking for support; “YouTube ignores typed text” is more useful than “nothing works”.

You can use the phone-side route below while you investigate. Repeatedly pairing the same TV is unlikely to tell you more once navigation already works.

## Choose the video on your phone

On the same Wi-Fi, open YouTube on both devices. Search on your phone, select a video, then use **Cast** in its player to choose the TV. Android 17 and later also require YouTube’s local-device discovery permission. [YouTube’s Android casting instructions](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/7640706?co=GENIE.Platform%3DAndroid&hl=en)

This route suits a particular episode, tutorial or music video you want to inspect on the phone first. Check the title and channel before sending it, especially when several videos have similar names. If other people are using the TV, check the destination before you interrupt their video.

If the TV is missing from the Cast list, YouTube also offers [TV-code linking](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/7640706?co=GENIE.Platform%3DAndroid&hl=en). You’ll need access to YouTube’s settings on the TV to obtain its code.

## Search while something is already playing

YouTube’s same-account companion experience lets you look for another video on the phone while the TV keeps playing. Its September 2026 update removed the shared-Wi-Fi and manual-connection requirements for that experience. Sign into the same Google Account on both devices. [TeamYouTube’s companion announcement](https://support.google.com/youtube/thread/463959026/use-your-phone-as-a-companion-for-watching-youtube-on-tv?hl=en)

That is a YouTube feature. A separate local-network remote still needs its own connection to the TV. Keep that distinction in mind if YouTube can see a screen that another remote app can’t find.

## The Remote: start with the query

The Remote includes a dedicated YouTube search entered with your Android phone keyboard and sent to your selected TV over the local network. It is for compatible Android TV and Google TV devices with Android TV Remote Service v2. The TV model and YouTube version determine whether the action is accepted. [The Remote’s requirements](https://baagad-ai.github.io/TVRemote-site/#compatibility)

The [phone-side search demo](https://baagad-ai.github.io/TVRemote-site/#search-proof) shows where you enter the query. If a query doesn’t arrive on your TV, check the selected destination, then try a search directly in the TV’s YouTube app. If that also fails, resolve the TV-side issue first. If YouTube works but the remote query fails, record the TV model, YouTube version and a harmless sample query for support.

The Remote needs no app account. [Download The Remote APK](https://baagad-ai.github.io/TVRemote-site/#download) when available. No signup or email is needed. Check compatibility before installing; a phone remote still needs a reachable TV on your home network.
summary: Choose where you want to browse the results.

title: Open a YouTube link on Android TV from your phone
description: Already have a YouTube link? Open it on your TV with YouTube’s connection options or review the link and destination in The Remote Android beta.
body:
# Open a YouTube link on Android TV from your phone

If you already have the video’s link, open it in the YouTube app on your Android phone and connect to the TV. The Remote offers another route for compatible Android TV and Google TV devices: share the link, review the destination, then choose the **Open** action for your selected TV.

You don’t need to type the title into the TV and hunt for the same video again.

## Use YouTube for a link you already have

Open the link in YouTube’s Android app, with YouTube open on the TV and both devices on the same Wi-Fi. Tap **Cast** in the video player and choose the TV. Mobile-browser YouTube doesn’t support this route; Android 17 and later need local-device discovery permission. [YouTube’s Android casting instructions](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/7640706?co=GENIE.Platform%3DAndroid&hl=en)

For different networks, use YouTube’s TV code: display it under **Settings → Add a device** on the TV, then enter it through **Cast → Add a device** on the phone. Tap **Link** and select the device. [YouTube’s code-linking guide](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/7640706?co=GENIE.Platform%3DAndroid&hl=en)

Check the title and destination before sending it. You’ll need an existing way to open the TV’s settings for the code route, so it isn’t a shortcut around an unconfigured or unreachable TV.

## Use The Remote’s share-and-review route

This route is for people who already have The Remote installed. You need an Android phone, a compatible Android TV or Google TV device with Android TV Remote Service v2, and a paired TV reachable on your local network. YouTube behaviour depends on the TV and its YouTube version. [The Remote’s requirements](https://baagad-ai.github.io/TVRemote-site/#compatibility)

### Share one video

Use the Android sharing option for the video or its link and choose The Remote. The share control’s location depends on whether you start in YouTube, a browser or a messaging app.

Share the video link itself. If a conversation contains several videos, choose the one you want first; a screenshot or whole conversation doesn’t identify the destination video reliably.

### Check the link and the screen

Review the link and selected TV in The Remote. If you’ve saved several TVs, pick the room where you want to watch. Check that another person isn’t using that screen before you send anything.

If you copied the link from a conversation, check it against the original message before continuing.

### Open it on the selected TV

When the link and destination are right, tap the **Open** action for that TV. The action sends the supported YouTube link to the selected compatible device.

Check the TV for the result. Its YouTube app, signed-in account and the video’s availability still determine playback. Your phone’s account, captions and playback position may not carry over.

## If it stops along the way

**The TV isn’t available:** check the saved destination and home-network connection. If the TV still remembers an old Wi-Fi network, restore its connection before trying again.

**The shared item isn’t accepted:** open the original video in the YouTube phone app and use the connection route above. URL formats can differ: a working ordinary video link doesn’t establish that Shorts, playlists or timestamp parameters behave the same way.

**YouTube opens but the video doesn’t play:** read the message on the TV. A sign-in request, unavailable video or playback error needs resolving there before sending the link again.

**The wrong TV received it:** check that screen before retrying elsewhere. Correct the selected destination before the next **Open** action.

## Give the link a destination

A shared video deserves a quick check before it reaches a bigger screen. The Remote keeps that choice explicit: review the link, choose the TV, then send it.

The Remote needs no app account. [Download The Remote APK](https://baagad-ai.github.io/TVRemote-site/#download) when available. No signup or email is needed. Check compatibility before installing; a phone remote still needs a reachable TV on your home network.
summary: Give a video you already found the right destination.

title: Lost your Android TV remote? What works before buying another
description: Lost your Android TV remote? Try a phone remote, check the old-Wi-Fi trap, and find safe, model-specific options before buying a replacement.
body:
# Lost your Android TV remote? What works before buying another

If your Android TV or Google TV is already connected to your home network, try the Google TV app on your Android phone. If the TV still remembers an old Wi-Fi network, or is waiting for first-time setup, a local-network remote app may not be able to reach it. Start with the branch that matches your screen.

## First, check whether your remote can ring

Have a Google TV Streamer and its paired Google TV Streamer Voice Remote? Briefly press the button on the back of the Streamer. The remote should sound for 30 seconds. Press any button on the remote once you find it. This button method is specific to the Streamer and its paired Streamer Voice Remote. Follow Google's [Find My Remote instructions](https://support.google.com/chromecast/answer/15322770?hl=en-GB), and don't hold the button down.

## The TV is already on your home network

Use Google's phone remote first:

1. Turn on the TV. For a separate streamer, select its HDMI input.
2. On the same home Wi-Fi, open the Google TV phone app and choose the TV from its connection button.
3. Enter the TV’s code, tap **Pair**, then try moving the TV selection.

See [Google’s pairing instructions](https://support.google.com/androidtv/answer/6122465?hl=en) if the app’s labels differ.

If the TV doesn't appear, check the simple things before changing settings: is the TV awake, and is your phone on the usual home Wi-Fi rather than mobile data or a guest network? If you can already see the TV's network status, compare it with your phone's connection.

For an unresponsive Google TV, unplug it for 10 seconds, reconnect, then retry pairing. Follow any different manufacturer instructions and let updates finish first. See [Google's virtual-remote troubleshooting](https://support.google.com/googletv/answer/15766805?hl=en).

### Both devices have internet, but they still can't connect

Internet access doesn't prove the devices can reach each other locally. Guest and managed networks may separate devices. Google identifies client isolation and sign-in-page networks as problems for its streaming devices. On a hotel, office or shared network, ask the owner which connection supports your device. Don't disable network security to make a remote app work. [Google's network guidance](https://support.google.com/chromecast/answer/7566322?hl=en-CA)

## You moved home or changed the Wi-Fi

This is the awkward loop: the TV needs a controller to join the new network, while your phone needs a reachable TV before it can act as that controller. Installing more local-network remote apps won't connect the TV to the new Wi-Fi for you.

Look for a control route that doesn't depend on that connection:

- **Buttons on the TV.** Check your model's manual for the power button or control panel and what it can operate. Some controls offer more than power; others don't. Sony's [remote troubleshooting guide](https://www.sony.com/electronics/support/articles/00030297) includes checking the TV's own buttons.
- **The television's remote, if you lost a streaming-box remote.** If HDMI-CEC control is supported and already configured, the TV remote may operate the connected device. Check both manuals. Sony calls its implementation [BRAVIA Sync](https://helpguide.sony.net/tv/nusltn1/v1/en-003/print.html); that example doesn't establish support for every TV-and-box combination.
- **A USB keyboard you already own.** Check the manufacturer's accessory guidance before trying it. Sony says many USB keyboards are recognised by its Google TV and Android TV models, while warning that functions can vary. That's a possible route on supported hardware, not a guarantee of full menu control. [Sony keyboard guidance](https://www.sony.com/electronics/support/articles/00128141)

Once one of these controls works, use the TV's network settings to join your current home Wi-Fi, then retry phone pairing. On Google TV, look under **Settings → Network & Internet**, as described in [Google's connection checks](https://support.google.com/googletv/answer/15766805?hl=en).

Ethernet may also be an option when the device has a supported port or adapter and can join your home network. For example, Google documents [Ethernet for its streaming devices](https://support.google.com/chromecast/answer/10109908?hl=en). A cable doesn't guarantee that phone pairing or unfinished setup will work. Check the exact hardware before buying an adapter.

## The TV is on a setup screen

Follow the instructions for that model and the screen you're actually seeing. Google offers [phone-assisted setup on supported Google TV devices](https://support.google.com/googletv/answer/10050221?hl=en), but its setup sequence can still require a paired remote before the phone takes over. A QR code setup option and an everyday phone remote are different stages.

Avoid a factory reset as a lost-remote shortcut. Google warns that resetting its streaming devices erases data and cannot be undone. You may end up back at setup with the same missing controller. [Google's reset warning](https://support.google.com/chromecast/answer/6254654/how-to-factory-reset-your-chromecast-android?co=GENIE.Platform%3DAndroid&hl=en-SG)

If none of the supported routes is available, borrow or buy a remote confirmed for the exact model. Check the model label on the TV or streaming box, then use the manufacturer's replacement and pairing guidance. A matching brand name alone isn't enough.

## Set up a backup while you have control

Once the TV is reachable again, pair your phone and check the controls you rely on. Keep the physical remote available for setup and any functions your phone can't operate.

Want to try The Remote as another phone-control option? It's for Android phones and [compatible Android TV or Google TV devices](https://baagad-ai.github.io/TVRemote-site/#compatibility) on the local network. The Remote needs no app account.
